Budget-Friendly Family Getaways: 5 Deals That Actually Deliver

by L.A. Family Travel | Aug 3, 2026 | Family Travel Deals

(This article may contain affiliate links. What does that mean?)

 

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:47
Instaread

Summer’s not over—it’s just transforming into that beautiful window when kids have already burned through their screen time allowance, parents are desperate to feel like heroes, and the deals get good. Whether you’re looking to splash through one final water park weekend, trade the heat for mountain air, lounge at an all-inclusive where kids stay free, or actually feel cultured at a winery with grape-stomping included, this roundup has the deals that make family vacations feel less like “how much did we spend?” and more like “remember when we did that?”

Each of these packages is live right now — some expire fast, some run through the holidays. Pick your vibe and book before the inventory runs out. Because the best family vacation isn’t the fanciest one; it’s the one you can actually afford without eating ramen for six months.

 

Great Wolf Lodge’s $84 Flash Sale: One Day Only

Somewhere, a marketing person looked at the number 84 and leaned all the way in. Great Wolf Lodge keeps its indoor water parks at a permanent 84 degrees — no sunscreen negotiations, no weather app anxiety — so every August 4, rooms drop to $84 a night.

That’s real savings: standard rates run $250–$400+ in peak season, and wristbands cover the water park from open on check-in day through close on checkout day. The $84 covers two guests; additional kids are $20 each, putting a family of four around $124 before tax.

The catches: book August 4 only using code 84DEGREES, travel Sunday–Thursday through December 17, no holidays, nonrefundable. Taxes, parking, and MagiQuest cost extra.

Valid at all 22 U.S. locations, including Anaheim — here’s our full weekend at Splashing Around at the Great Wolf Lodge Anaheim With Kids, wolf ears and all.

 

Wolf ears perked for this deal. Photo by Rina Nehdar

 

Antlers at Vail’s School is OUT and Vail is IN Summer Package

School’s out, and the Antlers at Vail is ready with a family-friendly deal: the School is OUT and Vail is IN package starting at $460 plus tax through August 31, 2026.

Two nights includes everything you need to actually relax: a custom map of the Antlers’ favorite Vail parks, bike rentals for four people, a custom picnic lunch, complimentary covered parking, and (the kicker) zero resort fees.

The real magic? Condo-style rooms with full kitchens, year-round heated pools and hot tubs, private balconies with propane grills, and a Pantry of home essentials to borrow. There’s even a one-bedroom-plus-bunkbeds option built for families of four who want space without the two-bedroom price tag.

You’re steps from Gore Creek path, Vail Mountain Resort’s gondola rides and hiking, and Lionshead Village’s shops and restaurants. Book online at antlersvail.com or call 888-268-5377.

Looking to maximize your Vail days? Here’s What To Do For Three Fun Days In Vail With Kids Who Love Adventure.

 

Climb every green mountain! For less!

 

Velas Resorts Summer: Kids Stay Free, Parents Stay Sane

Velas Resorts across Mexico just made summer vacation happen: kids stay free all summer long at properties from Los Cabos to the Riviera Maya (and teens are 50% off because apparently parenting teenagers deserves a discount).

The lineup is ridiculously good—Michelin-starred dinners at sea, taco masterclasses, science labs, a “Summer Olympics” complete with team challenges, even a Jungle Kids Spa for the little ones. At Grand Velas Los Cabos, there’s a Mini Velas City role-play for younger kids and a Star Chefs Michelin dinner aboard a private yacht. Grand Velas Riviera Maya just launched a new Kids’ Club with screen-free activities, alebrijes painting, and piñata-making. Velas Vallarta teaches kids golf fundamentals.

Throw in spa credits, guaranteed upgrades, and deals on airport transfers, and you’re basically getting paid to take your family to Mexico.

Bookings through August 31, 2026. Details at velasresorts.com/the-ultimate-playcation.

Planning a Riviera Maya trip? Read Grand Velas Riviera Maya Mexico: Celebrating Jewish Holidays In A Beachfront Resort to see what to expect.

 

Many luxurious options at a great deal. Photo courtesy of Velas Resorts

 

Loews Little Legends: STEAM Explorers Turns Hotel Stays Into Discovery Adventures

Forget the hotel room as a place to crash. Loews just launched Little Legends: STEAM Explorers, a summer program that transforms downtime into actual learning—the kind kids don’t complain about because, well, they’re too busy exploring to notice.

Here’s the kit: binoculars, compasses, magnifying glasses, kaleidoscopes, and activity books designed to make kids want to observe and experiment instead of scroll. It’s screen-free curiosity dressed up as fun.

On-property, partnering museums bring the science to life: Loews Miami Beach teams with the Frost Science Museum and FocalPoint for hands-on photography and science workshops. Loews Arlington partners with the Arlington Museum of Art for free classes ages 6–12.

The goal is multigenerational travel that feels intentional without feeling like work. Book at participating Loews properties nationwide.

Ready to dive in? See what to expect at Florida: The Loews Miami Beach Hotel and South Beach with Kids.

 

Hunting for the best kidsprieces. Photo courtesy of Loews Hotels

 

El Cielo Resort & Winery’s Harvest Season: 30% Off, Grape Stomping Included

Harvest season just became your excuse to actually do something active on vacation. El Cielo Resort & Winery in Valle de Guadalupe is marking August and September with a month-long celebration that is chef’s kiss — literally, because The Palm (the Presidente InterContinental’s iconic steakhouse) is setting up a guest restaurant on-site through August 23.

Book through September 29 for travel through December 16, and snag up to 30% off stays plus daily breakfast, 10% spa discounts, free bike rentals, early check-in, and late checkout. Access all the harvest programming included: master classes on Chardonnay, Tempranillo, and Mexican wine history; sunrise vineyard blessings; family grape-stomping; and full-day immersive harvest experiences. Kids get dedicated weekend activities (Saturdays and Sundays), and there’s Iberian ham pairings, vertical tastings, and a vineyard dinner under the stars.

Book at elcielovalledeguadalupe.com.

For multigenerational wine country trips elsewhere, check out Our 10 Favorite California Wine Festivals!

Dreaming of the savings. Photo courtesy of El Cielo Resort & Winery
